papers.titleEn: Integrated Capillary-Flow-Driven Paper-Based Microfluidic Sensor and ChromaSense Lab Mobile Analytical Platform for Quantitative Detection of 6PPD in Stormwater Runoff
papers.abstract: Abstract N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) is a widely used tire anti-degradant that is continuously released into the environment through tire wear and serves as the primary precursor to 6PPD-quinone, a transformation product associated with aquatic toxicity. Current determination of 6PPD primarily relies on laboratory-based chromatographic techniques requiring expensive instrumentation, specialized facilities, and trained personnel, limiting their suitability for rapid field deployment. Here, we report an integrated smartphone-assisted capillary-flow-driven paper-based microfluidic platform for quantitative detection of 6PPD in stormwater and roadway runoff. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first paper-based microfluidic platform developed for 6PPD analysis. The platform combines a capillary-flow-driven colorimetric sensor with ChromaSense Lab, a smartphone-based analytical platform that integrates image acquisition, flexible region-of-interest selection, quantitative color analysis, calibration generation, concentration prediction, and data export into a unified mobile workflow. Under optimized conditions, the sensor exhibited a linear response over the concentration range of 0−400 ppm with limits of detection and quantification of 9 ppm and 30 ppm, respectively. Calibration curves generated using ChromaSense Lab demonstrated excellent agreement with conventional ImageJ analysis (R2 = 0.993 and 0.995, respectively), validating the accuracy of smartphone-based quantification. The platform showed minimal interference from common inorganic ions and surfactants, maintained stability for at least four weeks under refrigerated and frozen storage conditions, and achieved recoveries generally within 80−120% with relative standard deviations within 10% in tap water, river water, and lake water samples. The sensor also achieved an AGREE greenness score of 0.81, demonstrating strong adherence to green analytical chemistry principles. By combining the first paper-based microfluidic sensor for 6PPD with a general-purpose smartphone analytical platform, this work establishes a rapid, portable, and user-friendly framework for decentralized screening of tire-derived contaminants in stormwater and roadway runoff. Although demonstrated for 6PPD detection, ChromaSense Lab was designed as an analyte-independent analytical platform and can be readily adapted to a broad range of paper-based, lateral flow, and other colorimetric sensing applications.

papers.titleEn: Managing the Spatial Interactions of Ligands on Perovskite Quantum Dot Films for Efficient Photovoltaic Devices
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Although perovskite quantum dot (PQD) photovoltaics have evolved swiftly, the stability of their devices still lags far behind that of their polycrystalline counterparts, which limits our understanding of how to modulate the spatial interactions of novel, highly stable ligands in PQD thin films to maximize their photophysical performance. Herein, using the fluorine‐rich moiety pentafluorobenzyl as a template, O‐(2,3,4,5,6‐pentafluorobenzyl)hydroxylammonium (5FBHA) as a post‐synthetic ligand was discovered to interact spatially uniformly with PQD films, owing to its visualized high‐density stable binding fashion on the PQD surface. Compared to its analogue 2,3,4,5,6‐pentafluorobenzylphosphonic acid, 5FBHA resulted in an improved packing mode for its treated PQD film, which further benefited charge‐carrier dynamics and enhanced moisture stability. Notably, the best‐performing rigid and flexible CsPbI 3 PQD solar cells treated with 5FBHA achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 16.21% and 14.37%, respectively, and demonstrated enhanced stability under long‐term operation (degradation rate: 0.13% h −1 vs 0.25% h −1 for the control one) and N 2 ‐storage conditions (remained 96.8% of the initial value vs 88.6% for the control one). This work poses a logical chemistry design principle that correlates the ligand interaction mode to PQD properties, and facilitates the advancement of promising PQD optoelectronics.
papers.filename: Jun Xi, Small, 2026, Managing the Spatial Interactions of Ligands on Perovskite Quantum Dot Films for Efficient Photovoltaic Devices

papers.titleEn: Radiation-Crosslinked Relaxor Ferroelectric Elastomers for Fully Organic Stretchable Capacitive Strain Sensors
papers.abstract: The adaptation of capacitors to wearable electronics requires dielectric materials that combine high permittivity with well resilience. Fully organic stretchable capacitive strain sensors are particularly attractive, but their performance is often limited by the lack of suitable elastic high-k dielectrics. Relaxor ferroelectric polymers offer intrinsically high dielectric constants; however, conventional elastification approaches, such as thermal and photo-crosslinking, are constrained by harsh processing conditions and residual chemical species. Here, we present a simple and effective radiation-crosslinking strategy to convert a relaxor ferroelectric polymer into an elastic dielectric without the need for initiators or elevated temperatures. By employing poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene-chlorofluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE-CFE)) in combination with poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) as a crosslinking sensitizer, a stable crosslinked network is formed under mild irradiation conditions. The resulting material exhibits a high dielectric constant (∼37 at 25°C and 1 kHz) together with excellent elastic recovery (∼80%), thereby achieving a desirable balance between dielectric performance and resilience. When integrated with stretchable electrodes, the resulting fully organic capacitive device exhibits reproducible capacitance variation to tensile strain, demonstrating its potential for fully organic stretchable capacitive strain sensing. This work establishes a practical strategy for developing high-permittivity dielectric elastomers and advances the design of stretchable electronic devices.
papers.filename: Benlin Hu, Small, 2026, Radiation-Crosslinked Relaxor Ferroelectric Elastomers for Fully Organic Stretchable Capacitive Strain Sensors
